Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal Order on Board (10.05.2024)
1.

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, against the award
dated 28.03.2016 passed by the learned Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bilaspur,
District - Bilaspur (C.G.), in Claim Case No. 224/11 ("Deva Yadaw Vs. A. Madhav Rao & Ors.")
whereby an amount of Rs. 47,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum has been awarded in favour of
the appellant herein for his irreparable loss.

entities.text: Deva Yadaw Vs. A. Madhav Rao & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2.  The averment in the claim petition, in brief, was that Appellant-Dewa Yadav, who was aged aged about 25 years and was working as Dairy employee and on 14.01.2011 appellant along with co-employee-Nand Kumar Yadav was returning from dairy farm and when they reached near Sakri High School, the biker Nand Kumar stopped the bike to check air in a shop, at the same time respondent No. 4 driving the motorcycle bearing Registration No.-C.G.-11-B- 0211 (offending vehicle) in rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle of the Nand Kumar on which the appellant was also riding as a pillion rider, as a result of which the appellant-Dewa Yadav suffered grievous injuries and sustained bone fracture on his femur.
He underwent Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17183 treatment.
Crime No. 38/11 was registered in Police Station- Chakarbhata.

3. It is stated by the appellant that he was working in Shri Sai Dairy Needs under the respondent No.
1-A. Madhav Rao and he was earning Rs. 3,300/- per month, due to the said accident he has suffered physical and mental agony and also spent money on his treatment.
Therefore, he had filed a claim application before the Tribunal under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act against the respondents claiming total compensation of Rs. 11,50,000/-.
4. The Tribunal, in the absence of any documentary evidence thereof regarding income of the claimant, has taken his income as Rs. 3,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has held that the permanent disability has not been proved by the appellant but the fact of his receiving grievous injury on account of the said accident has been proved.

On the basis of overall evidence, Rs. 12,000/- towards loss of income, Rs. 10,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs. 5,000/- towards transportation and Rs.
20,000/- towards treatment expenses in future.
Thus, a total compensation of Rs. 47,000/- has been awarded in favor of the Appellant.
The driver Nand Kumar has not been made party before the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has not found any rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle Nand Kumar in which the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17183 appellant was sitting as a pillion rider.
The offending vehicle which was being driven by respondent no.4 Saransh Mathur was not insured.
Hence, the respondent Nos. 3 & 4 were held liable to pay the compensation amount to the appellant who were owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

2 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant argues that the appellant was admitted in the hospital for about 9 days (i.e. from 17.01.2011 to 26.01.2011) and underwent treatment and suffered mental agony for a long time.
The awarded compensation by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Therefore, the appeal is liable to be allowed and the compensation amount may be enhanced suitably.

6. No one appeared for respondent No. 1.
7.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 2 to 4 supported the impugned award and submit that the award in question is based on proper appreciation of material available on record, therefore, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

8. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.

From the perusal of the entire material available on record, it is clear that the Appellant was admitted in the hospital for about 9 days (i.e. from 17.01.2011 to 26.01.2011) and underwent treatment, due to the bone fracture on his femur but the permanent disability has not been proved by the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17183 appellant by producing any documentary evidence.

Dr.
Vinod Tiwari (AW-2) has been examined on behalf of the appellant who states that on 15.01.2011 the appellant was admitted to his hospital and had bone fracture on his femur.
They operated the bone on 17.01.2011 by inserting a rod and discharged him on 26.01.2011 (discharge ticket Ex.P- 4).

This witness in his statement has not stated the fact that the injury to the left thigh of the appellant has caused him any kind of permanent disability, rather he has denied the fact that due to the fracture of the thigh bone, the man would be handicapped for the rest of his life.

Thus, looking to the evidence of doctor who examined the appellant, the awarded amount of Rs. 12,000/- towards loss of income, Rs. 10,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs. 5,000/- towards transportation and Rs.
20,000/- towards treatment expenses in future is just and proper.
However, in my opinion, it is appropriate to award an additional compensation of Rs. 10,000/- towards inconvenience in future due to said injury and Rs. 10,000/- towards special diet and attendant.

10. Thus, looking to the entire facts and circumstances of the case, an additional amount of Rs.
20,000/- is hereby enhanced.
11. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
The claimant shall be entitled to Rs. 20,000/- in addition to what is already Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:17183 awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount will carry interest @ 6% from the date of enhancement of the award till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the above extent and rest of the conditions shall remain intact.

12. The Registry is further directed to communicate the claimant in writing "the enhanced amount"
in this appeal as against the award made by the Tribunal below.

The said communication be made in Hindi Deonagri language and the help of paralegal workers may be availed with a co- ordination of Secretary, Legal Aid of the concerned area wherein the claimants resides.
